To confirm the band alignment between the 2D and 3D perovskites, we conducted ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) on half devices FTO/SnO2/perovskite/2D. We treated the 3D perovskites with ligands solution of different concentrations. We measured SEM to confirm their surface coverage and UPS to confirm their band alignments to the 3D perovskite. In Figure 1.7 a, b, c, as the concentration of the ligand solution increases, we observe a more complete 2D perovskite coverage. With incomplete 2D coverage (1mM and 2.5mM), UPS shows that the treated sample has a deeper valence band compared to the 3D perovskite without treatment. The valence band position at -6.4eV coincides with that of lead iodide, which suggests IPA Page 15 of 54 DE-EE0009512 Massachusetts Institute of Technology dissolves the surface and leads to more exposed lead iodide. In the case of 5mM and 10mM, we observe the 2D perovskites have a type II alignment to the 3D perovskite, where hole can be selectively transferred into 2D perovskites. We conclude that at higher concentrations the formation of 2D perovskites dominates. Data in Figure 1.7 fulfills partly Milestone 1.1.3. We fabricated devices to demonstrate correlation between the 2D coverage and thickness and device performance. In Figure 1.8, there is a positive correlation between the 2D thickness and device performance. When treated with Hexane-1,6-diammonium bromide, we observed a slight decrease of efficiency compared to the untreated device at 1mM, consistent with the UPS measurement that the band alignment is unfavored for hole transfer. As we increase the concentration of the ligand solutions to 2.5mM and 5mM, we observe an increase of efficiencies compared to the untreated samples. The best device reaches 21% compared to 19.5% for the untreated devices.
